'''''Narcissus triandrus''''', also known as the '''Angel's Tears daffodil''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] within the family [[Amaryllidaceae]].

The popular [[cultivar]] 'Hawera', belonging to the Triandrus group, has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-20 |title=Narcissus 'Hawera' (5) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/95558/narcissus-hawera-(5)/details |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=[[Royal Horticultural Society]]}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Narcissus triandrus'' is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant]]. The bulbs of this species are small and dark in colour.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Köhlein, Menzel |first=Fritz, Peter |title=Color Encyclopedia of Garden Plants and Habitats |publisher=Timber Press |year=1994 |isbn=9780881922981 |pages=206}}</ref> Bulbs lay dormant in the soil for the majority of the year until emerging in the Spring. A single bulb usually produces two leaves each that can grow to a length of {{Convert abbreviated|20|cm}} long by 4–5 mm wide. Leaves are keeled, striate on their surface and sometimes coiled at the tip.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-06-20 |title=Narcissus triandrus |url=http://encyclopaedia.alpinegardensociety.net/plants/Narcissus/triandrus |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=[[Alpine Garden Society]]}}</ref> Stems of the species are {{Convert abbreviated|30|cm}} tall, thick, tubular, and almost waxy on their outer side.<ref name=":12">{{Cite book |last=Burbidge |first=F. W. |title=The Narcissus: Its History and Culture with Coloured Plates and Descriptions of All Known Species and Principal Varieties |publisher=L. Reeve & Co. |year=1875 |location=Henrietta Street, London |pages=57–58}}</ref> Stems can hold from one to six cup-shaped flowers, which are milk white or pale yellow in colour.<ref name=":0" />

== Reproduction ==
The flower size varies, increasing from southeast to northwest, correlating with plant size, probably reflecting a rainfall gradient from the hot [[Mediterranean climate]] of the southeast to the cooler, wetter Atlantic climate found in the northwest. Changes in flower size correlate with pollinator fauna, ''[[Anthophora]]'' species being dominant in the southern population and the larger-bodied ''[[Bumblebee|Bombus]]'' species in the north.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Barrett, Harder |first=Spencer C H, Lawrence D |date=2022-06-20 |title=The evolution of polymorphic sexual systems in daffodils (Narcissus) |journal= New Phytologist|volume=165 |issue=1 |pages=45–53|doi=10.1111/j.1469-8137.2004.01183.x |pmid=15720619 }}</ref>

[[Self-pollination]] was found to result in significantly lower seed production than in [[cross-pollination]] within ''Narcissus triandrus''.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Sage |first1=Tammy L. |last2=Strumas |first2=Fanny |last3=Cole |first3=William W. |last4=Barrett |first4=Spencer C. H. |date=1999-06-01 |title=Differential ovule development following self- and cross-pollination: the basis of self-sterility in Narcissus triandrus (Amaryllidaceae) |journal=American Journal of Botany |language=en |volume=86 |issue=6 |pages=855–870 |doi=10.2307/2656706|jstor=2656706 |pmid=10371727 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
Native to [[France]], [[Spain]] and [[Portugal]],<ref name="Narcissus triandrus L">{{Cite web |date=2022-06-20 |title=Narcissus triandrus L. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:66256-1 |access-date=2022-06-20 |website=powo.science.kew.org}}</ref> where it grows in woodlands, scrubland and exposed mountain habitats in acidic soils.<ref name=":0" />

It has been observed to grow in scrublands, mesophilic grasslands, sandy soils, including some more rocky areas. In Europe, the plant has been spotted in the [[Iberian Peninsula]], the Iberian and Aracena Mountains, as well as the Baetic and Penibaetic mountain systems and the Serra de Monchique.<!-- Reference? -->

== Cultivation ==
[[File:Narcissus 'Thalia'.jpg|thumb|[[Narcissus 'Thalia'|''N. triandrus'' 'Thalia']], a variety that bears open, nodding flowers]]
While not a very popular species of the daffodil, these plants have similar care and blooming needs.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Triandrus Narcissus Group |url=https://www.gardenia.net/plant-variety/triandrus-narcissus-group |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=Gardenia.net}}</ref> They are low maintenance plants that require full sun, or part shade, medium water (meaning that the soil should be watered until damp, then left to dry and once dry, watered lightly again).<ref name=":3" /> The species is tolerant of rabbits, deer, and drought.<ref name=":3" /> This aversion towards disease and pests is known to be from the plant's high alkaloid and lycorine content.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Narcissus triandrus (Orchid Daffodil) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/narcissus-triandrus/ |access-date=2022-04-15 |website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref>

Flowering in late spring, April through May, it is best that these plants are planted above summer blooming buds, yet below early spring bloomers.<ref name=":4" /> It is suggested that these plants be potted or placed in soft, well drained ground in late fall.<ref name=":3" /> If planted deep enough (two to three times deeper than the bulbs original length) then it should retain its moisture and last through the winter.<ref name=":3" /> And, while these flowers do like shady areas, it is better for them to be placed in full sun or in an area that gets sun throughout most of the day, this is because of the flowers of like to point towards and be in the sun's light as much as possible.<ref name=":3" />
